title: The First Big Computer Weighed 30 Tons and Used 18,000 Tubes

scenes.text: The first big electronic computer weighed 30 tons.
ENIAC had about 18,000 glowing vacuum tubes.
It filled a room 30 by 50 feet and used 150 kilowatts of power.
Tubes kept burning out, sometimes several in a single day.
Even so, it worked out a missile's path in 15 seconds.
That job took a human several weeks.
Thirty tons. Slower than your phone.

description:
The first big electronic computer weighed 30 tons.
ENIAC used about 18,000 vacuum tubes and 150 kilowatts of power. At its public demonstration it calculated a missile trajectory in 15 seconds, a job that would have taken a human several weeks.
What would you do with a 30-ton computer? Comment below.
